note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: CORRECTION (Oct 21): no US shutdown — Trump signed the CR Sept 2, funded through Dec 11; Sept jobs/CPI/PPI/housing all printed on schedule (the 'shutdown day 20' line was bad data). France: revenue-section vote postponed (first reading to Oct 27; FinMin Lescure floated Article 49.3); 2,828 of 3,396 amendments unexamined; OAT-Bund ~157-160bp Wednesday (widest since the 2009-11 crisis); OAT 10Y 5.00% (first since Jul 2002); Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 neg, one-notch cut to A1 expected). UK: Sep borrowing £24.5B miss (vs £23.9B); debt >£3T; Healey Budget Oct 28.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US: housing soft patch (starts 1.221M miss, pending home sales -7.3% record low, ADP 18.5K) vs last week's retail (+0.8%) and IP (+0.7%) beats. Japan: Sep exports +16.7% missed (+20.1% exp); 5th straight trade deficit. China: Q3 GDP 4.5% beat.
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: UK Sep CPI verified 3.5% y/y beat (vs 3.4% fcst; highest since Oct 2025 on energy; core 2.8% in line; services 3.7% sticky; PPI +4.6% vs 4.3%) — reinforces the priced Nov-5 BoE path, no repricing (Reuters/WSJ verified). German Sep PPI +6.7% y/y beat (vs 6.2%). US CPI 3.7%, PPI hot; import prices +8.1% y/y. NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (0.8% q/q, 3.8% y/y fc; RBNZ proj 3.9%).
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: FOMC Oct 27-28: hold ~83-84% (FedWatch via Reuters, Oct 21; Kalshi 89%) — blackout, no speakers; December hike ~90%. BoC Oct-28 hike ~90-95% (CORRA OIS 95%); RBNZ ~80-81% to 3.00% (Dec second hike ~50%; Q3 CPI tonight the decider). ECB Oct 29: hold virtually certain (70/73 economists); Dec hike ~88%. BoE Nov 5: ~96-98% post-CPI ('nearly fully pricing in'); Dec back-to-back ~61% pre-CPI. RBA Nov 2-3: ~40% (from ~30%). BoJ Oct 29-30: 'virtually no chance' of a hike; Dec ~73-74%.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). Crowded trades are fragile: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: New CFTC (Oct 13 report): all G10 signals neutral (0). Splits: hedge funds flipped AGAINST the yen while real money bets FOR it; hedge funds for the Aussie but real money strongly against. Funds strongly short CAD (added sharply). No crowded-long unwind risk anywhere — the pain trade is two-sided.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: DXY drifting on UK/NZ inflation and steady yields — no haven bid (contradictory Houthi/Saudi drone claims: Houthis deny Medina drones, coalition says intercepted; Iran-Pakistan mediation chatter). France protests + curfews (~550k marched Saturday); euro the drag.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent ~$110 (Asia +1.1%; Tuesday $112→$106 on unconfirmed Qatar/Pakistan mediation, then retraced — headline-driven). WTI ~$99-102 (front-month/Dec quotes mixed across sources). Gold ~$4,118 — 4th down day, trading Dec-hike odds (~90%) not oil headlines.
tot.title: Terms of trade
